📝 Phonics Rules & Patterns

Master the patterns that help you read new words!

Vowel Teams (Two Vowels = One Sound)

When two vowels sit together, the first one speaks and the second is silent!
ai, ay
/eɪ/ rain, day
ee, ea
/i/ tree, sea
oa, oe, ow
/oʊ/ boat, toe, grow
oi, oy
/ɔɪ/ coin, boy
ou, ow
/aʊ/ loud, cow
ue, ui
/u/ blue, suit

Magic E (Silent E Rule)

When 'e' is at the end, it makes the vowel say its LONG sound and stays silent!
a-e
cake /eɪ/
e-e
Pete /i/
i-e
pine /aɪ/
o-e
note /oʊ/
u-e
tube /u/

Consonant Blends (Two Sounds Blend Together)

Both consonants make their sounds - they blend smoothly together!
bl, cl, fl
black, clap, fly
br, cr, dr, fr, gr, pr, tr
bring, cry, drop, frog
sc, sk, sl, sm, sn, sp, st, sw
scan, skip, slip, snap, star
ck, nd, nt, st
back, hand, mint, fast

Digraphs (Two Letters = ONE Special Sound)

Two letters make a brand new sound - NOT a blend!
sh
/ʃ/ shop, fish
ch
/tʃ/ chop, beach
th
/θ/ or /ð/ the, think
wh
/w/ or /hw/ whale, who
ph
/f/ phone, photo
ng
/ŋ/ ring, sing

R-Controlled Vowels (R Changes the Sound)

When R follows a vowel, it CHANGES the vowel sound completely!
ar
/ɑr/ car, star
er, ir, ur
/ɝ/ her, bird, fur
or, ore
/ɔr/ for, more
ar
/ɑr/ care, dare

🎵 Six Syllable Types

Understanding syllables helps you read longer words!

Type 1: CLOSED Syllable

Consonant + Vowel + Consonant (CVC) = SHORT vowel
cat
short a /æ/
nap-kin
closed
hap-py
closed
rab-bit
closed

Type 2: OPEN Syllable

Consonant + Vowel (CV) = LONG vowel sound
go
long o
ba-by
open
ti-ger
open
ho-tel
open

Type 3: SILENT E Syllable

CVC + E = LONG vowel sound (E is silent)
cake
long a
bike
long i
hope
long o
tube
long u

Type 4: VOWEL TEAM Syllable

Two vowels together = ONE long sound
rain
ai team
beach
ea team
boat
oa team
play
ay team

Type 5: CONSONANT + LE Syllable

C + LE at end = schwa sound /əl/
ta-ble
-ble
ap-ple
-ple
can-dle
-dle
pur-ple
-ple

Type 6: R-CONTROLLED Syllable

Vowel + R = R changes the vowel sound
car
ar /ɑr/
her
er /ɝ/
bird
ir /ɝ/
for
or /ɔr/

Syllable Reference Chart

Type Pattern Vowel Sound Example
🔒 Closed CVC SHORT cat, napkin
🔓 Open CV LONG go, baby
✨ Silent E CVCe LONG cake, hope
👥 Vowel Team VV ONE rain, beach

📋 Complete Phonics Reference Guide

All 26 Letters - Quick Reference

Vowels (5): A /æ,eɪ/ • E /ɛ,i/ • I /ɪ,aɪ/ • O /ɑ,oʊ/ • U /ʌ,u/

Consonants (21): B C D F G H J K L M N P Q R S T V W X Y Z

Key Phonics Rules

1. CVC Pattern: Consonant-Vowel-Consonant = Short vowel sound (cat, bed, pig)

2. Magic E Rule: CVC + E = Long vowel sound (cake, hope, tube)

3. Vowel Teams: Two vowels = One sound (rain, beach, boat, coin)

4. Blends: Two consonants = Both sounds blend (black, crisp, stand)

5. Digraphs: Two letters = One special sound (shop, chip, think)

6. R-Controlled: Vowel + R = R changes the sound (car, her, bird)

7. Soft C: C says /s/ before E, I (city, cent) but /k/ before A, O, U (cat, cut)

8. Soft G: G says /j/ before E, I (gem, gist) but /g/ before A, O, U (go, gum)

6 Syllable Types

1️⃣ CLOSED: CVC → Short vowel (cat, napkin)

2️⃣ OPEN: CV → Long vowel (go, baby)

3️⃣ SILENT E: CVCe → Long vowel (cake, hope)

4️⃣ VOWEL TEAM: VV → One sound (rain, beach)

5️⃣ C+LE: C+LE → Schwa sound (table, apple)

6️⃣ R-CONTROLLED: VR → R changes sound (car, bird)

Common Vowel Sounds

Short Vowels: /æ/ (cat), /ɛ/ (bed), /ɪ/ (sit), /ɑ/ (hot), /ʌ/ (bug)

Long Vowels: /eɪ/ (cake), /i/ (tree), /aɪ/ (like), /oʊ/ (go), /u/ (blue)

Learning Tips 💡

1. Sound Out Words: Say each sound, then blend them together smoothly
2. Use Hand Motions: Move your hand as you say each sound
3. Read Aloud: Hearing words reinforces the patterns
4. Practice Daily: Even 10 minutes a day builds strong skills
5. Use Context: Look at pictures and meaning to guess words
6. Identify Syllables: Look for vowel sounds to find syllable breaks
7. Master Patterns: Focus on one pattern at a time (CVC, then Magic E, etc.)
8. Review Regularly: Keep reviewing earlier patterns as you learn new ones

Word Building Strategy

Step 1: Identify each letter
Step 2: Say each sound
Step 3: Identify syllables (look for vowel sounds)
Step 4: Determine syllable type for each (Closed? Open? Silent E?)
Step 5: Say the vowel sound for that type
Step 6: Blend all sounds together smoothly
Step 7: Say the whole word!
